estimates.outcome: Desktop-VR operative skill test (0-100, auto-scored by the VR system, taken unassisted within 15 min after 1-week training)
estimates.treatment: ChatGPT-3.5 as a supplementary instructor added to instructional videos (free version; used during a 1-week skill-acquisition period to resolve doubts, verify procedures, and give extra guidance)
estimates.notes: ChatGPT-3.5 (free version) added to instructional videos vs identical videos only (blank control); ChatGPT is the sole additive difference. Raw operative-test scores 73.12 (SD 10.06) vs 65.54 (SD 12.48) on a 0-100 auto-scored desktop-VR task; mean diff 7.58 points, Welch t(176.24)=4.569, P<.001. N=187 analyzed (192 recruited, 5 excluded at eye-tracking calibration; 94 ChatGPT vs 93 control). Baseline theoretical-knowledge test balanced (41.24 vs 42.03, P=.52). No AI during the test (design inference; the paper does not explicitly state ChatGPT was blocked at test). Cohen's d=0.669, SE=0.150, 95% CI ~0.38-0.96 back-calculated from per-arm means/SDs/n; no author-reported standardized effect. Effect concentrated among low-spatial-ability students (70.20 vs 55.41, P<.001) and absent among high-spatial-ability students (76.58 vs 73.89, P=.22). Secondary outcomes favored ChatGPT: self-efficacy P=.04, learning motivation P=.02, cognitive load via pupil-diameter change 0.137 vs 0.312 P<.001.
estimates.estimation_method: Independent-samples Welch t test on post-test desktop-VR operative scores, t(176.24)=4.569, P<.001 (normality checked via Shapiro-Wilk); complete-case on the 187 students who passed eye-tracking calibration. Cohen's d and its SE (0.150) back-calculated from reported per-arm means, SDs, and n; no author-reported standardized effect.

estimates.outcome: IRT-scaled endline math assessment (Oxford MeasurEd), unassisted; intent-to-treat
estimates.treatment: Gemini "Guided Learning" integrated by teachers into half of weekly math lessons (~12h over 8 weeks, students in pairs)
estimates.notes: Table C.4 col 2 (baseline-adjusted ANCOVA); the paper's headline intent-to-treat estimate, in SD units of the IRT-scaled endline math score. Stored Ns are the analyzed balanced panel (present at both baseline and endline), N=1,423 = 712 treatment + 711 control (Table C.2); the enrolled sample of 1,763 appears on the study card. (Previously stored n_total was the enrolled 1,763; corrected in the 2026-07 W. Erda verification rount); baseline N=1,547, endline N=1,637. 95% CI [0.027, 0.488], p=0.029. Unadjusted ITT = +0.216 SD (SE 0.137, not significant); fully adjusted (adds gender, age) = +0.259 SD (95% CI [0.025, 0.494], p=0.031). Authors benchmark 0.258 SD as roughly 1.2-1.7 years of extra learning in LMICs and a 50th-to-60th percentile move. Gemini 2.5 Pro for first six weeks, 3.0 Pro for final three weeks. Uptake: 69.0% of the 871 treatment students reached the requested 12h; treatment classrooms averaged ~15h. Field monitors (one per school, 12 total) documented no spillover beyond two isolated incidents, and any spillover would attenuate the estimate. Heterogeneity: effect rises +0.195 SD per baseline-math SD (p=0.002), favoring higher-baseline students.
estimates.estimation_method: OLS with baseline math+reading scores, block FE; SE clustered at classroom (48 clusters)
